subject: Re: Addendum Review: tiered throughput & fallback path
messages:
From: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@velocitech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+contracts@velocitech.com
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Addendum: tiered throughput and pricing — redlines

Hi Kimberly / Jordan,

Thanks for sending the draft order form this morning. We've run it by our procurement and legal team and attached a marked-up PDF with a handful of redlines and comments. High-level asks from our side:

- Flatten the SLA termination notice from 60 to 30 days for pilot tiers.
- Add an explicit fallback path if a dedicated capacity pool is unavailable: temporary burst credits + automatic downgrade to a compatibility model without degrading response guarantees.
- Clarify invoicing cadence for tiered throughput (we prefer monthly in arrears rather than upfront quarterly).
- Ensure data retention for logs is at least 12 months for auditability (SOC artifacts).

I'm looping in our legal contact Sarah Kline (cc'd) for any contract language specifics. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the fallback language and the 30-day pilot termination? If not, please propose alternate wording we can review.

Attachment: VelociTech_OrderForm_Draft.pdf (annotated)

Best,
Emily Ramos
Head of Cloud Procurement, VelociTech
ops+contracts@velocitech.com

On Tue, Sep 1, 2027 at 08:05, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Forwarding initial draft as discussed during demo.

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: (none)
Date: 2027-09-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Addendum: tiered throughput and pricing — redlines

Laura / Jordan,

FW: VelociTech's annotated order form. They tightened a couple things that are reasonable but the fallback wording and the 30-day termination request will need legal's quick take.

Proposed commercial stance from Sales:
- Accept 30-day termination for the pilot tier only (not for committed Dedicated capacity). Document as "Pilot tier: 30-day opt-out" in Exhibit A.
- For the fallback path, offer a measured approach: automatic temporary burst credits (up to X tokens/min) + downgrade to a lower-cost model variant with a documented maximum latency delta, for a defined window (up to 72 hours) while we remedy capacity.
- Move invoicing to monthly arrears for the pilot tier; committed capacity stays quarterly as-is.

Can you draft two short contract options we can send to Emily: (A) clean acceptance with minimal edits and (B) counter-proposal that preserves our SLA and cost protections but addresses their main asks. Need these by EOD so I can coordinate a call with VelociTech tomorrow.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: KP_annotated_addendum_redlines.docx)

Cc: legal_ops@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Addendum: tiered throughput and pricing — redlines

Kimberly / Jordan,

Thanks for the context and the annotated doc — good summary. I reviewed VelociTech's marked-up PDF and drafted two short options as requested. Key legal notes below:

Option A (accept with edits) — customer-friendly, faster close
- We can accept a 30-day termination right limited strictly to the "Pilot" product SKU; add language that any committed Dedicated pool, pre-paid credits, or reserved nodes are excluded.
- Fallback path: we will add a defined "Fallback Procedure" clause in Exhibit B that authorizes temporary burst credits (capped) and an automatic, time-limited downgrade to a compatible model variant. We must include explicit wording: "Redwood will endeavor to restore provisioned capacity within 72 hours; if restoration requires changes to pricing, Redwood will notify Buyer and provide a remediation plan."
- Data retention: 12 months for request/trace logs is acceptable; will add a carveout limiting log contents to metadata (no user PII).

Option B (counter-proposal) — protects platform economics and SLA
- Keep default termination at 60 days for all service tiers but offer a 30-day pilot opt-out as a commercial concession with a one-time exercise right during month one of the pilot.
- Fallback: prefer a human-in-loop escalation (notify ops + customer) before automatic downgrades; offer automatic downgrade only if customer explicitly opts in and accepts a capped per-token surcharge during fallback window.
- Invoicing: can move pilot tier to monthly arrears; committed capacity remains quarterly.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Send Option A as the fast path and mark Option B as our fallback if VelociTech needs to preserve protected rates.
2) Include a short Annex that defines: "pilot SKU", "fallback window", "burst credit cap (tokens/min)" and an example calculation for remediation charges.

If Sales is comfortable, I can produce a tracked-change Order Form (Option A) by 5pm PT. Otherwise indicate which names/terms you'd like tightened.

- Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Quoted below is Emily's original note for thread context.

From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ramos <emily.ramos@velocitech.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+contracts@velocitech.com
Date: 2027-09-01T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Addendum Review: tiered throughput & fallback path

Hi Emily — appreciate the quick review and clear asks.

Kimberly and I talked this through with legal (Laura) and we're going to ship Option A as the primary path — it's the fastest and addresses your top items while keeping our operational protections. Laura will attach a tracked-change Order Form (Option A) in a follow-up email by 5pm PT today.

For transparency on the fallback mechanics: we'll propose the following wording in Exhibit B, "Fallback Operations and Temporary Capacity Credits":
- Automatic temporary credits equal to up to 48 hours of median pilot throughput at no charge (standard per-token accounting applies after the free window).
- Automatic model-compat downgrade only if the Buyer opts in; otherwise Redwood will initiate ops-level failover and provide a remediation timeline (72 hours target).

Would you be open to a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to finalize the wording and sign-off? If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and include a short slide showing the fallback flow and example billing calculation.

Thanks — Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success & Renewals, Redwood Inference

VelociTech (external) replied to confirm availability and asked for the tracked changes.
